note: Four dimensions, keyed and kept apart. An entry point is HOW a journey starts; an evidence source is WHERE the journey was derived from; a recovery path is WHICH named record proves a recovery journey exists. Conflating any two of them lets a derivation launder its own provenance, so the census validator rejects a journey that reuses an id across dimensions.

entryPoint.name: Canonical pipeline
entryPoint.description: The documented ladder in CLAUDE.md §Workflow / §Entry Points: the user names the next skill in the intended order (grill → to-prd → to-issues → implement → wrapup).

entryPoint.name: Goal-level delegation
entryPoint.description: The user states an OUTCOME, not a skill, and the agent must self-route. #343 seed 7.

entryPoint.name: Question turned work
entryPoint.description: A session opens as a question ('why is this red?', 'does X hold?') and becomes work mid-conversation, with no skill invoked at the boundary.

entryPoint.name: ask-matt routing
entryPoint.description: The user does not know which skill fits and asks the router; the router names a starting point.

entryPoint.name: Direct skill invocation
entryPoint.description: The user types the slash command for one skill, out of any pipeline order.
entryPoint.evidence: .claude/skills/skill-manifest.json — 44 publishable skills, each description naming its own trigger

entryPoint.name: Externally created worktree or session
entryPoint.description: The session starts in a worktree or on a branch the session itself did not create — an orchestrator's subagent, a resumed handoff, a manually created worktree.

entryPoint.name: Codex-surface entry
entryPoint.description: The same system entered through the second surface: .agents/skills/ read by a Codex session. A mirror is the same journey through a different door, not a second journey.
entryPoint.evidence: 37 of 44 logical skills carry a codex surface (skill-manifest.json); .agents/skills/

evidenceSource.name: Installer CLI commands
evidenceSource.description: The command verbs src/cli.mjs dispatches on.

evidenceSource.name: update / uninstall / diff
evidenceSource.description: The three consumer-reconciliation verbs #380 §5 names separately from the rest of the CLI, because the consumer contract lives on them.

evidenceSource.name: Package lifecycle scripts
evidenceSource.description: npm scripts a maintainer or CI runs.

evidenceSource.name: GitHub workflows
evidenceSource.description: Automation that runs without a session attached.

evidenceSource.name: Agent hook events
evidenceSource.description: The 24 shipped hooks and the agent events they bind to. Activation is consumer-owned — this repository ships the hook files and wires only .githooks/, so a hook is a promise a consumer may or may not have switched on.
evidenceSource.query: for f in .claude/hooks/*.py; do grep -m1 -o 'SessionStart\|PreToolUse\|PostToolUse\|UserPromptSubmit\|Stop' $f; done | sort | uniq -c

evidenceSource.name: Board status and label vocabulary
evidenceSource.description: The lifecycle path encoded in the board profile; no single skill covers it end to end.

evidenceSource.name: Issue and pull-request history
evidenceSource.description: The empirical record of journeys actually taken.

evidenceSource.name: Shipped skill descriptions
evidenceSource.description: Each publishable skill's description names its own trigger, and a trigger is an entry.

evidenceSource.name: The .agents/ surface
evidenceSource.description: The second door into the same system. Divergence from the primary is a finding on the primary, not a second artifact.

evidenceSource.name: Named recovery records
evidenceSource.description: Recovery-labelled or recovery-titled issues, pull requests recording a STOP and re-run, retro findings, and documented recovery paths. Bounded by construction (#380 §5).

recoveryPath.name: Pull request recording a STOP and a re-run
recoveryPath.recordSource: aggregate-queries.json — merged-pr-retro-marker rows with a findings heading

recoveryPath.name: Retro finding in a merged pull-request body
Recovery path documented in a shipped skill or in CLAUDE.md
recoveryPath.recordSource: git-worktree-recover, resolving-merge-conflicts, kit-release §red run, kit-update; CLAUDE.md §Prod

recoveryPath.name: unknown-recovery
recoveryPath.recordSource: None. Exhaustiveness of the recovery set cannot be proven, so a recovery journey with no record in the sources above is classified here rather than omitted or invented. The sources searched are exactly the four above; nothing else was consulted.
